scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated from the Lindy Hop around 1920 and evolved through the Boogie Woogie of the 1940s.
By 1955, as rock music gained popularity, the dance shifted toward a competitive, acrobatic style.
In the 1970s, French dance schools in Lyon formalized the discipline, leading to the creation of the World Rock'N'Roll Confederation (WRRC).
on_screen: Map: United States (origin), France (modern sport development) · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is primarily a competitive sport.
It is performed at local, national, and international championships organized by the WRRC.
The focus is on precision, athleticism, and the execution of high-difficulty acrobatic elements.
Today it remains a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance relies on a 6-basic or 9-basic step structure.
The 9-basic step is the modern tournament standard, featuring a kick-ball-change maneuver.
Dancers move in a linear fashion, maintaining a precise, upright posture while executing kicks into the air.
Watch for Einsteiger and Körperwelle.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (uvbLjBYyQ3c)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Linear movement, pairs or formation groups.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to 4/4 time music, typically modern disco or pop tracks played at high speeds between 176 and 208 bpm.
The rhythm emphasizes the first and third beats of each measure, differing from the off-beat stress of traditional rock music.
Listen for modern pop and disco instrumentation.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 192 beats a minute.
A high-tempo, driving beat provides a clear, consistent pulse to support rapid footwork and athletic movement.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear custom-made, multicoloured costumes crafted from elastic, durable artificial fibers.
The costumes are tight-fitting to prevent snagging during acrobatics.
Footwear consists of light jazz shoes for dance programs or aerobics sneakers for acrobatic programs to provide grip and shock absorption.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Notable figures include French world champion Miguel Angueira and Katerina Tikhonova.
Categories are divided by age and skill level, including Youth, Juniors, and Main Class Contact Style and Free Style.
The lineage runs from Swing in the 1920s to Lindy Hop, Boogie Woogie in the 1940s, and Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll from 1955 to the present.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is the parent of the Lindy Hop, the foundational swing dance from which acrobatic elements were first introduced.
Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is the parent of Boogie Woogie, a faster adaptation of swing that bridged the gap to rock music.

scenes.title: Welcome
narration: Chapter 1 covers first steps and mastering the 6-basic step.
The level is beginner, while the overall dance difficulty is advanced.
Your instructor is an experienced competitive coach with a background in dance sport.

narration: Posture is upright, precise, and athletic.
The body is active, used for balance and partner connection.
Movements are controlled, utilizing specific body wave motions to initiate lifts.

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
